I will think this through the way I always do, starting from what I did last year.

My 8.5 mu — I split it like before. About 5 mu goes to wheat in winter, then maize after. The other 3.5 mu I keep for cotton, same as always. Cotton brings cash, the grain feeds us and what we don't eat we sell.

For the wheat, I use the same seed the shop sells, the one everyone around here plants. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer before I plough — that's about 100 jin per mu — and then one bag of urea when I water in spring. My neighbor Old Wang puts less but his yield is always a little worse, so I don't cut back. Better to spend a few extra yuan than watch the wheat turn yellow. I water three times — before winter, at jointing, at filling. If the well is busy I skip one but usually three.

For the maize after wheat harvest, I plant the hybrid seed from the same shop — everyone buys that one. I don't plough, just push the seed in with the machine right after wheat. I put urea twice, maybe 40 jin each time at the roots. I water twice if the rain is bad, sometimes just once. Maize doesn't need as much fuss as wheat.

Cotton is the hardest. Bugs come every year and if I don't spray they eat the bolls. I spray maybe six times, whenever I see them. I put fertilizer heavier on cotton because the plants are big — two bags compound at planting, urea when they flower. I plough the cotton land properly, cotton doesn't do well in hard ground.

Money is tight with just me and my wife, so I count every bag. But I never skimp on fertilizer at planting — once the crop is short of food you can't fix it.
